sections.content: How many people are "metal making and treating process operatives"?

14,390 people

were counted on the census as "metal making and treating process operatives" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Metal making and treating process operatives operate furnaces, ovens and other heating vessels, drawing, rolling, extruding, galvanising, forging and other metal processing equipment to smelt, shape, coat and treat metal and metal products.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "metal making and treating process operatives" there were more men than women (90.7% compared with 9.3%).

This means "metal making and treating process operatives" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "process, plant and machine operatives".

Men made up 90.7% and women made up 9.3% of "metal making and treating process operatives"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "metal making and treating process operatives" included:

  • train and tram drivers
  • engineering technicians
  • precision instrument makers and repairers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "metal making and treating process operatives" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "metal making and treating process operatives", 13.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "metal making and treating process operatives" was 16 to 19 years.

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "metal making and treating process operatives", 8.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (91.6% compared with 8.4%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (90%) than self-employed (10%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the West Midlands. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Sheffield, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
